Answer: C
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates bilateral, relatively symmetrical air-space opacities that are predominantly distributed in the mid and lower lung zones with relative sparing of the apices. This pattern is characteristic of diffuse alveolar hemorrhage seen in Goodpasture's syndrome, distinguishing it from pulmonary edema (which typically involves the costophrenic angles) or pneumonia (which is often asymmetric or lobar).
